claude_proposed_widenings.name: assume_form
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape's core mechanic is the druid assuming a Beast form and having their game statistics replaced by the Beast's stat block. No v4 atom covers form transformation — neither 'alter_item_kind' (items only) nor any companion/summoning atom (those create separate entities rather than replacing the activating creature's statistics). This is a distinct transformation primitive.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; Hit Points; Hit Point Dice; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureActivationMechanics.duration
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape persists for a timed duration (hours equal to half druid level) with multi-condition early termination (re-use, Incapacitated condition, death, or voluntary Bonus Action exit). ClassFeatureActivationMechanics has no duration field. The activation family's current shape models only instantaneous effects; it cannot represent the lifecycle of an active form.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a Bonus Action.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: grant_temp_hp
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape grants Temporary Hit Points (equal to Druid level) when the form is assumed. Temporary HP are mechanically distinct from healing (they don't restore lost HP, don't stack with other temp HP, and expire on their own). The existing 'heal_hp' atom cannot represent this; it applies to restored HP pools, not the temporary HP buffer.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Druid level.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: assume_form duration: conditional_expiry with multiple triggers
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The form expiry has multiple simultaneous exit conditions: timed (N hours), event-based (re-use = self-break), condition-based (Incapacitated), state-based (death), and voluntary (Bonus Action exit). The existing lifecycle atoms (expire, self_break, dismiss) cover individual cases but there is no surface-level composition mechanism for a disjunction of expiry triggers on a class feature.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: ...until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a Bonus Action.
